newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends up, tracking NYMEX technical rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends up, tracking NYMEX technical rally.

text.p: IPE Brent rebounded off lows for the second time in the session on Wednesday to close higher as NYMEX futures led a late rally across the oil complex, brokers said.
Feb Brent closed 22 cents up at $23.91 a barrel, 70 cents off the intra-day low.
Brokers said the contract's roller-coaster ride on Wednesday was dictated by the movement of NYMEX crude, which rallied strongly triggering technical buying stops, rather than any fundamental news.
"There's no real reason for it. (NYMEX crude) kept pushing up, basically on technicals," a broker said.
Jan NYMEX crude futures bounced off support to end the day with a ferocious rally which broke through its post-Gulf War high of $26.10 a barrel, briefing touching a high of $26.22.
Weekly stocks data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) were seen as more bullish than API data released after the close of trade on Tuesday.
"The (EIA data) was pretty bullish, and even the APIs were less bearish than some people expected," a broker said.
The EIA reported a 400,000 barrel draw on U.S. distillate stocks last week, despite an increase in refinery output in most areas.

With forecasters predicting below-normal temperatures across the U.S. until the end of the weekend, the EIA data reinforced expectations of supply tightness in the key heating oil-consuming regions of the U.S., traders said.
The impact of the first sailings of tankers loaded with Iraqi crude from the Gulf was hard to assess, brokers said.
"Everyone says that (Iraqi exports) have been discounted, every time a step is taken it does have a psychological impact," said one.
Jan gas oil earlier closed $219.25 a tonne, down $2.75 on the day in thin volume after a brief spurt to the upside took the contract to a session high of $222.75.
Brokers said that trading volumes were thin leaving the market unstable and at the whim of NYMEX heating oil.
"The volumes have been a let down. We've basically been toyed with by the U.S." said a dealer.
Brokers said that some players were reluctant to take positions in such a volatile market.
"There's been a distinct lack of quality paper. In some cases management might have given orders to play down risk because the market is so erratic," said one.
